description: Agent Trust and Compliance. Five endpoints an autonomous agent can call before it trusts a counterparty domain or address, each backed by a real live check (no simulated or bundled-static data). POST /v1/domain-trust (domain): RDAP registration data + DNS (MX/SPF/DMARC/DNSSEC) -> a 0-100 trust score. POST /v1/brand-verify (domain, brand_name?): a live TLS certificate handshake -> validity, organization-validation, SAN coverage, and an optional brand-name match against the certificate identity. POST /v1/seller-trust (url): a composite of both for one resource-server URL, with a trusted/proceed_with_caution/high_risk recommendation. POST /v1/sanctions-check (address): the U.S. Consolidated Screening List (OFAC SDN + 10+ other restricted-party lists), requires an operator-supplied free API key. POST /v1/reputation (chain, address): an EVM address's on-chain activity/verification/scam-flag signal via public Blockscout explorer instances (eth, base, arbitrum, polygon). Every score is 0-100 with a 'reasons' array explaining exactly how it was computed. All outbound domain/IP lookups are guarded against private/loopback/link-local targets.

rpc_types.backend_hint: agent-trust HTTP server on :8080; mount at /
rpc_types.notes: Only POST /v1/domain-trust, /v1/brand-verify, /v1/seller-trust, /v1/sanctions-check, /v1/reputation, and GET /v1/version, /v1/health are expected. Every response is a JSON object; bad input (including an SSRF-guard refusal or an unconfigured operator API key) returns 4xx with a JSON error object, never HTML or plain text.

specs.notes: Covers all five resources in one document. TODO before MainNet staking: pin this to an immutable commit SHA in the path (not 'main') and add a sha256 of the exact bytes once frozen, per this repo's own README.

serving.backend: The agent-trust Node.js HTTP server (no external dependencies) behind a RelayMiner, with the REST backend pointed at http://<container>:8080. No auth toward the backend; callers cannot send headers through the gateway. The backend calls out to rdap.org, the domain/hostname under test itself (DNS + a live TLS handshake on :443), data.trade.gov (only if the operator has set TRADE_GOV_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY), and public Blockscout instances (eth/base/arbitrum/polygon .blockscout.com) — it needs broad outbound HTTPS/DNS/TLS access, not a fixed allowlist, since domain/brand-verify/seller-trust probe whatever domain the caller names (subject to the backend's own private-IP SSRF guard).

healthcheck.notes: Identity probe: pins the backend to this service so a wrong backend cannot be staked under this id.

Functional probe against example.com (IANA-reserved for documentation/testing, always resolvable). Proves the backend can reach RDAP and resolve DNS right now; example.com's real registration data changes rarely, but only the score's numeric shape is asserted, not a value, since it is a live computation.

serving.notes: Suppliers should disable any local rate limiting for the RelayMiner's address. Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB and responses are ordinarily a few KB. Backend timeout budget: keep well under the operator's configured relay_timeout (typically 10-30s); each upstream call has an 8s timeout with one retry, and DNS/TLS calls this backend makes to the caller-named domain are separately bounded to 8s. /v1/sanctions-check needs an operator-supplied free API key (TRADE_GOV_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY from https://developer.trade.gov) — without one it returns 422 not_configured rather than a false 'clean' result. Gateway operators: configure as type passthrough with rpc_types ["rest"]; see sage-service.yaml.
